title: Drift Response Hardening
depends_on: S213 Drift Simulation Results (4/6 detected, mean response quality 1.67/5, overall CONCERN)
objective: Close every gap S213 identified in drift detection, containment, and recovery. Build the complete Detect→Contain→Remediate→Prevent chain for all 6 drift categories. The S213 audit proved stewardship can detect 4/6 categories. S218 ensures it can detect, contain, and recover from ALL 6.

undetected_scenarios: Scenario 2: Shadow Queues (CLI bypassing governance guard)
Scenario 6: Untracked Artifacts (session packages invisible to dashboard)
pre_remediation_state.containment_capability: NONE — detection triggers reports, not automated containment
pre_remediation_state.remediation_capability: MANUAL — every remediation requires human-orchestrated agent chain
pre_remediation_state.prevention_capability: PARTIAL — governance guard prevents some write-level defects but has zero visibility into CLI/bash operations

drift_response_playbook.principle: For every drift category: DETECT automatically, CONTAIN immediately, REMEDIATE systematically, PREVENT permanently.

categories.description: Multiple registries tracking the same entity with divergent counts. S213 found 4+ competing question registries with 1,300-item variance.

detect.mechanism: Cross-registry reconciliation at session startup (T0) — compare counts across all registries claiming authority over the same entity class. Any divergence >0 triggers halt.
detect.implementation: Add to AGENTS.md §9 T0 protocol: (1) grep raw files for Certified count, (2) compare against CURRENT_BASELINES.md §2, (3) compare against MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md Certified column, (4) compare against SESSION_STATUS. Any discrepancy → halt and reconcile.
detect.governance_guard_rule: Rule 7 (proposed S217) — BLOCKs creation of competing registries

contain.mechanism: QUARANTINE the divergent registry — mark as STALE, prevent consumption by any downstream tool or dashboard until reconciled.
contain.implementation: At T0 detection of registry divergence: (1) log the divergence to a DRIFT_EVENT log, (2) set a STALE flag on the divergent file path, (3) all consumers check for STALE flag before reading. No tool may consume a STALE registry.

remediate.mechanism: Regenerate from authoritative source. The STALE registry is overwritten by regeneration from raw source files — not hand-patched.
remediate.implementation: Execute the registry's regeneration script (e.g., scripts/build_master_registry.js) from raw pack files. Verify post-regeneration count matches raw-file grep. Clear STALE flag on success.
remediate.automated: Semi-automated — regeneration is scripted but may require verification

prevent.mechanism: Rule 7 (DERIVED_REGISTRY_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE BLOCK) prevents any new script from creating a competing registry. Existing derived registries carry NOT_AUTHORITATIVE headers. T0 reconciliation catches divergence before it propagates.
prevent.implementation: Deploy Rule 7 to governance-guard.js. Add NOT_AUTHORITATIVE header to all derived registries. T0 protocol extension.

categories.description: Node.js scripts executed from CLI bypass governance guard entirely — can write to pack files, certify items, and modify registry data with zero enforcement. S213 Scenario 2: undetected.

detect.mechanism: File-hash monitoring at T0, Tmid, Tend checkpoints. Any unexpected hash change in a pack file or registry triggers immediate investigation.
detect.implementation: Per AGENTS.md §13.1 T0→Tmid→Tend checkpoint sequence: capture all 13 runtime hashes at T0. At Tmid and Tend, re-capture and compare. Any drift in a pack-file hash without a corresponding REVISION_HISTORY.md entry = Shadow Queue detection.
detect.governance_guard_rule: Hash comparison is run manually — governance guard does not currently have filesystem hash access

contain.mechanism: Diff the changed file against the last authorized backup. Identify the exact change (lines, fields modified). Quarantine any new certifications added outside the governance guard.
contain.implementation: At detection: (1) git diff or filesystem diff against last backup, (2) extract any new Certified question_state changes, (3) if any: set those items to HOLD state, (4) log to DRIFT_EVENT. Learner pool is protected because delivery mechanism reads from source files — revert before next learner session.
contain.automated: Semi-automated — diff is scripted, assessment requires audit

remediate.mechanism: Rollback to the last authorized backup if changes were unauthorized. If changes were legitimate but bypassed governance guard, retroactively create REVISION_HISTORY entry and re-run governance guard validation.
remediate.implementation: Restore from backup (BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md). Re-apply any legitimate changes through the governance guard. Run full validator suite before re-authorizing.
remediate.automated: Manual — requires orchestrator judgment on legitimate vs unauthorized

prevent.mechanism: No existing mechanism can prevent CLI-based Node.js writes to pack files — this is a fundamental OS-level limitation. Mitigation: (1) per AGENTS.md §2, all write tools are disallowed by default — only explicit authorization enables them, (2) backup-before-edit is mandatory (BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md), (3) T0→Tmid→Tend hash monitoring closes the detection gap, (4) Rule 7 blocks creation of new competing registries.
prevent.implementation: AGENTS.md §2 already in effect. T0→Tmid→Tend hash monitoring deployed. Rule 7 deployed.
prevent.note: Complete prevention of CLI bypasses would require OS-level mandatory access controls — out of scope for governance guard. The defense-in-depth approach is: T0→Tmid→Tend detection + backup-based recovery + AGENTS.md §2 read-only default.

post_remediation_coverage.prevent: PARTIAL — OS-level limitation, mitigated by defense-in-depth

categories.description: Multiple independent scan scripts produce divergent counts for the same defect. S213 found DL-008 counts of 10, 342, and 32 from three tools.

detect.mechanism: Cross-tool reconciliation gate: when two tools report different counts for the same metric, the discrepancy is flagged at write time.
detect.implementation: Any script that writes a defect-count claim to a JSON report must compare its count against the existing canonical count in DEFECT_MANIFEST_DL008_DL026.json. If counts diverge by >5%, flag a RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED status and block the write.
detect.governance_guard_rule: New rule: scan tools must consume DEFECT_MANIFEST as canonical count source — not independent re-scan

contain.mechanism: Quarantine the divergent scan result. Prevent it from being consumed by admin dashboards or pipeline tools until reconciled with the canonical count.
contain.implementation: Mark the report as DISPUTED_COUNT. Admin dashboards filter out DISPUTED_COUNT entries. Pipeline tools skip DISPUTED_COUNT reports.

remediate.mechanism: Independent third-agent verification using boundary-aware object parsing (the DL-029-safe method). This agent's count becomes the authoritative reconciliation.
remediate.implementation: Spawn an independent verification agent using Function constructor parse (not regex block-window). This is the only method proven to produce accurate counts (DL-029 resistant). Update DEFECT_MANIFEST with the verified count.

prevent.mechanism: All scan tools must use the SAME extraction methodology — boundary-aware object parsing (Function constructor or string-aware brace-matcher). Any tool using regex block-window or forward-scan methods is flagged as DL-029-vulnerable and blocked from writing counts.
prevent.implementation: Standardize on Function constructor parse for all defect-counting tools. Deprecate regex block-window scanning. Add parse-methodology validation to governance guard.

categories.description: Developer modifies a validator or governance guard to weaken a gate, enabling items to pass through that should be blocked. S213 Scenario 4: undetected.

detect.mechanism: CURRENT_BASELINES.md must include hashes for ALL governance-critical files — not just pack files. Validator source files, governance guard source, and build scripts all need baseline hashes.
detect.implementation: Extend CURRENT_BASELINES.md §4 to include: governance-guard.js hash, ExplanationValidator.js hash, build_master_registry.js hash, all test suite file hashes. At T0, verify all governance-critical hashes against baseline. Any unexpected change = potential manual workaround.

contain.mechanism: If a governance-critical file hash has changed: immediately halt all certification operations. Diff the file against backup to identify the change. If the change weakens any gate → quarantine all items certified since the change.
contain.implementation: At detection: (1) halt all certification, (2) diff changed governance file, (3) if gate was weakened: extract certification timestamps after change, (4) re-validate all affected items against pre-change validator.
contain.automated: Semi-automated — diff is scripted, impact assessment requires audit

remediate.mechanism: Restore the governance-critical file from backup. Re-run the full governance guard test suite (32/32 tests). Re-validate any items that passed through the weakened gate.
remediate.implementation: Restore from backup. Run test suite — must return 32/32 PASS. Re-validate affected items against restored validator. Any items that fail → revert certification.

prevent.mechanism: All governance-critical files are included in CURRENT_BASELINES.md with SHA-256 hashes. T0 hash verification catches changes before any certification work begins. The governance guard is self-protecting — its source code is a baselined file.
prevent.implementation: Add governance-critical files to CURRENT_BASELINES.md §4. T0 hash verification per AGENTS.md §13.1.

categories.description: REVISION_HISTORY claims do not match actual file state. S213 found 'UNCHANGED' claim that was false (28-item delta from S853 WAVE_A).

detect.mechanism: Automated count-delta validation: at every session close, compare the pre-session and post-session Certified counts from raw-file grep. If REVISION_HISTORY claims 'UNCHANGED' but counts differ → flag traceability break.
detect.implementation: At session close (Tend): (1) re-run raw-file grep for Certified count, (2) compare against pre-session count captured at T0, (3) if delta >0: verify REVISION_HISTORY entry exists and matches the delta, (4) if delta >0 and REVISION_HISTORY claims UNCHANGED or has no entry → BLOCK session close until traceability is restored.

contain.mechanism: If traceability break detected at Tend: session cannot close. The delta must be documented in REVISION_HISTORY with exact QID list, before/after counts, and certification session reference.
contain.implementation: BLOCK session close. Agent must: (1) document the delta QID list, (2) write REVISION_HISTORY entry with exact count change, (3) re-verify post-entry count matches raw-file grep.

remediate.mechanism: For past traceability breaks (S853 28-item delta): retroactively document the delta in REVISION_HISTORY with S853 WAVE_A attribution. The 28 items are legitimately Certified — the defect is in the documentation, not the content.
remediate.implementation: Append REVISION_HISTORY entry: 'S853 WAVE_A: 28 Domain E+F items certified (not documented in S263-S266 UNCHANGED claim). Corrected retrospectively 2026-07-27.'

prevent.mechanism: Rule 1 BLOCK upgrade: any question_state change without REVISION_HISTORY entry is blocked at write time. Automated count-delta validation at session close catches any that slip through.
prevent.implementation: Rule 1 upgraded to BLOCK. Tend count-delta validation deployed.

categories.description: Session packages, reports, and scripts written without registration. S213 Scenario 6: undetected — 729 session packages, only ~200 registered. 192 scripts, many undocumented.

detect.mechanism: Filesystem-vs-registry reconciliation: at session close, compare the count of files in scripts/output/session_packages/ against the session_registry.json entry count. Any file without a registry entry is an untracked artifact.
detect.implementation: At Tend: (1) count files in scripts/output/session_packages/, (2) count entries in session_registry.json, (3) if files > entries: list orphan files, (4) flag UNTRACKED_ARTIFACTS. Same for scripts/ vs SCRIPT_REGISTRY.json.

contain.mechanism: Orphan files (not in registry) are flagged and isolated. They are not deleted — content may be valuable. They are marked as UNREGISTERED and excluded from admin dashboard consumption until registered.
contain.implementation: At detection: (1) move orphan files to scripts/output/unregistered/ (preserving content), (2) log to UNTRACKED_ARTIFACT_LOG.json, (3) exclude from all dashboard and pipeline consumption.

remediate.mechanism: Register or retire each orphan file. Registration requires: file purpose, source session, QIDs affected, authority level. Retirement: archive the file and document why it was not registered.
remediate.implementation: For each orphan: (1) determine its source session, (2) determine if content is still relevant, (3) if yes: create registry entry in the appropriate registry, (4) if no: move to archive/ with a retirement note.
remediate.automated: Manual — requires inspection of each orphan file

prevent.mechanism: PRE-WRITE gate: any script that writes a file to scripts/output/session_packages/ must first verify a corresponding session_registry.json entry exists. Scripts cannot create untracked outputs.
prevent.implementation: Add pre-write hook to all output-writing scripts. The hook checks session_registry.json for the target session ID. If not found, write is BLOCKED.

Rule 4: WARN→BLOCK (detection for answer-key unauthorized changes — categories 4, 5)
Rule 7: NEW — BLOCK (detection for duplicate registries — category 1)
Rule 8: NEW — BLOCK (detection for unregistered artifact creation — category 6)

CURRENT_BASELINES.md §4: add test suite file hashes (category 4 defense)
